findings.evidence: previous-version digest at dbff837f: "removed units (394, showing 40)". All 40 shown items, and both items in the d4ad4291 digest, have valid rows in docs/audit/recovery/professional-communication/record.md. The other 354 could not be checked.
findings.fix: Rerun the removal check with the full unit list, or confirm that every one of the 394 para: ids maps to a section row in docs/audit/recovery/professional-communication/sections.json that has a valid row in record.md. Restore any unexplained unit (into references/ when it is domain-specific or a template users ask for), or add a row for it to docs/audit/recovery/professional-communication/record.md.

findings.evidence: "Three golden rules: a clear subject or purpose, scannable formatting (bullets, headlines), and the key message first." The model applies this unprompted. The audience line 25 ("identify recipient, desired outcome...") is also mostly activation.
findings.fix: Keep the What-Why-How definition: the record row s022 says compose-email and the coach agent depend on it. The golden-rules sentence is already in README.md (§ Three Golden Rules), so it can move there: delete it from SKILL.md and add a para: row to docs/audit/recovery/professional-communication/record.md. Use the freed line for a non-obvious rule, such as when What-Why-How gives way to impact-first ordering.

findings.evidence: "## Route by goal" gives the fields for each message type but no drafting sequence: no gather facts → pick channel → choose ordering → draft → check unknowns.
findings.fix: Add a 4-step sequence above Route by goal: (1) list the supplied facts and mark unknowns, (2) pick the channel with the lightest-channel rule, (3) pick the ordering (What-Why-How by default, impact-first for escalations), (4) draft, then check every date, number, owner and promise against step 1.

findings.evidence: "Never send incident urgency through an unmonitored channel" and "Do not paste credentials, customer data, or sensitive logs into broad channels" state no reason or failure mode, and reviewers would call them obvious.
findings.fix: Give each item the failure it prevents. Example: "Never route incident urgency through a channel nobody is paged for: a post in #eng at 02:00 can sit unread until morning while the on-call pager stays silent." Add gotchas this skill really meets, with their reasons. Example: forwarding an internal thread to an external stakeholder exposes the earlier internal discussion below the new message.

findings.evidence: The description does not mention the restored scope (standups, retrospectives, 1:1s, code review walkthroughs, review/help/intro emails, team norms). It gives no implicit triggers and does not draw a line against the near neighbours writing-clearly-and-concisely and feedback-mastery.
findings.fix: Draft and improve software-team emails, Slack/Teams messages, stakeholder status updates, escalations, review or help requests, meeting agendas (standup, sprint planning, retrospective, 1:1, design or code review), meeting summaries and team communication norms. Use when translating technical work for non-technical audiences without inventing metrics, making an async request actionable, choosing a channel across time zones, or structuring a project update, even if the user only says 'make this clearer' or 'tell the execs'. Not for performance-review coaching or difficult feedback (feedback-mastery), sales copy, legal documents, sentence-level style edits (writing-clearly-and-concisely), or actually scheduling meetings.

findings.evidence: The Route by goal bullets (Escalation, Status update, Request) do not point to the matching template. Only the separate "Load by deliverable" section at line 38 does, and it is keyed to "Before sending email", so an escalation drafted for Slack may skip references/email-templates.md.
findings.fix: Add the load trigger to each route bullet. Example: "Escalation: ... Use the Escalation pattern in references/email-templates.md for email or chat." Do the same for Status and Decision request.

findings.evidence: Should-trigger queries are terse fragments with no context ("Escalate production issue; lead with impact."). Several negatives test nothing ("Fictional dialogue between coworkers.", "Translate paragraph from French to English.", "Personal thank-you note to family member."). No query covers standups, retros, 1:1s or team norms. In evals.json, "Audience calibrated and outcome explicit" is not verifiable.
findings.fix: Replace the three far-off negatives with near-misses: a sentence-level style edit (writing-clearly-and-concisely), giving a peer difficult feedback (feedback-mastery), and a README/API doc. Rewrite 4 positives with realistic context (names, paths, a pasted draft), including one each for a 4Ls retro agenda and team response-time norms. Split the vague agenda assertion into "Names who attends from product and engineering" and "Final agenda item states the decision outcome".

findings.evidence: "Organize any message as What ... Why ... How" conflicts with line 16, "Escalation: lead with user/business impact", and line 21, "lead with impact and end with the single decision needed". For an escalating request, the What-first frame and the impact-first route give different orderings, and the skill does not say which one wins.
findings.fix: State the precedence in the Frame section: "What-Why-How is the default; for escalations, lead with impact (Why), then the decision needed (What), then mitigation and owner (How)." Add a final check line: "Before returning the draft, check every date, number, owner and promise against the facts supplied, and mark the rest Proposed: or unknown."
